normalized.description: Objectives: To develop affordable, re-usable aerodynamic shapes involving the re-entry of upper stages of launchers. Description: The use of ceramics and metallic materials on aerodynamic shapes for reusable systems technology allows for affordable and sustainable operations involving the re-entry of upper stages of launchers. This study aims at designing and prototyping the shapes with an appropriate material combination that can survive the mechanical stresses induced in the initial ascent and can subsequently survive the extreme heating and mechanically shear environment of re-entry. Also it conducts ground based experimental tests for a relevant flight profile and advances the numerical prediction of gas surface interactions. This activity is building upon a previous TDE activity on the recovery of upper stage launchers (T418-703MP) as well as the Space Rider Programme.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition, of the descent system requirements and the trade space to be examined for materials with suitable coatings and aerodynamic shapes: - Performance analysis conducted to define the pressure and shear environment with emphasis on re-usability. - Numerical modeling and prediction of the surface catalysis for multiple flights. - Design and prototype the aerodynamic shape system for a typical upper stage recovery of small and large European launchers like Ariane next and/or VEGA-E using numerical investigations as a basis. - Perform plasma testing in relevant pressure and shear environments, supported by rebuilding and extrapolation to flight. - Evaluation of test results. - Development of a roadmap for technology maturation and guidelines for future applications. Provision for inputs for a possible future handbook.
